subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted-owner approval-bypass mode for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and should it live as a shared execution policy instead of a Telegram-only boolean?
rationale: Source inspection proves the requested mode is absent, but deciding when an operator identity may skip approvals changes a security boundary and config surface that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

options.title: Keep existing approval model
options.body: Decline the bypass and document that operators who want no prompts should use existing elevated/full and host approval policy settings deliberately.

options.title: Add Telegram-only shortcut
options.body: Implement the proposed Telegram config directly, accepting a narrower patch but higher long-term drift risk from shared approval and elevated execution semantics.

recommendation.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product/security boundary decision before Telegram and approval owners can implement a safe shape.
